allergen = a substance that can cause an allergic reaction
halal = prepared according to Islamic rules, especially of meat
kosher = prepared according to Jewish dietary law
corkage = a fee for bringing your own wine into a restaurant
house wine = the restaurant's ordinary, usually cheaper wine
processed food = food that has been changed from its natural state, often with additives
food waste = edible food that is thrown away instead of being eaten
organic = produced without synthetic pesticides or fertilisers
fair trade = a system that aims to pay producers in poorer countries a fairer price
food security = reliable access to enough safe, nutritious food
food miles = the distance food travels from where it is produced to where it is eaten
factory farming = keeping large numbers of animals in intensive conditions for cheap meat or eggs
farm-to-table = food served soon after it is grown, with few middlemen
battery farming = keeping hens in small cages to produce eggs cheaply
free-range = allowed to move outdoors, especially of hens or their eggs
animal welfare = the health and living conditions of animals kept by humans
livestock = farm animals such as cattle, sheep and pigs
genetically modified = having genes changed in a laboratory to give a plant or animal new traits
food additive = a substance put in food to colour, preserve or flavour it
superfood = a food marketed as especially rich in nutrients
